rows.Description: Apply filters to extract only relevant objects, geometry, or metadata. For example: ifcClass = 'IfcDoor' from IFC files, category == 'Wall' from Revit models, or custom property-based filters.
Extracted data is stored as a standalone exchange, significantly reducing file size and complexity while maintaining data integrity.

Each exchange has a unique ID and lifecycle, enabling updates, tracking, and reuse across project phases. For example, a “Structural Elements” exchange might evolve from initial design (version 1) to design development (version 2) to construction documents (version 3) as the project progresses.

Exchanges can be consumed in multiple applications, for example: Autodesk products (Revit, Civil 3D, Inventor), third-party applications (Rhino, Grasshopper), and custom applications via API. See the Data Exchange Roadmap for available connectors.
Create exchanges manually through the user interface or automate creation using GraphQL mutations for scalable, repeatable workflows.

rows.Exchange Solution: An architect needs to share only the structural elements (beams, columns, foundations) with a structural engineer. Instead of sending the entire 500MB Revit model, they create a lightweight exchange containing just structural components.
A mechanical engineer shares HVAC equipment and ductwork with a fabrication shop. The exchange excludes architectural elements, focusing only on components that need to be manufactured.
A design team shares only exterior walls, windows, and doors with a facade consultant. The consultant gets exactly what they need for their specialized review.
A quantity surveyor receives room data, dimensions, and material properties in a lightweight exchange for accurate cost calculations—no need to open the full architectural model.
Teams using different software (Revit + Tekla, or Rhino + Inventor) share compatible data through standardized exchange formats.
